definitions.gloss: timbre; tone color; the distinctive quality of a sound
definitions.explanation: The characteristic quality of a musical sound that distinguishes different instruments or voices, even when playing the same pitch at the same volume.

examples.japanese: このピアノは{美|うつく}しい{音色|ねいろ}だ。
examples.english: This piano has a beautiful tone.

examples.japanese: バイオリンの{音色|ねいろ}に{惹|ひ}かれた。
examples.english: I was captivated by the violin's timbre.

examples.japanese: {楽器|がっき}によって{音色|ねいろ}が{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Each instrument has a different tone quality.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{声|こえ}は{温|あたた}かい{音色|ねいろ}がある。
examples.english: Her voice has a warm tone.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {美|うつく}しい{音色|ねいろ}: beautiful tone
- {温|あたた}かい{音色|ねいろ}: warm tone
- {澄|す}んだ{音色|ねいろ}: clear tone
- {独特|どくとく}の{音色|ねいろ}: distinctive timbre
- {音色|ねいろ}を{奏|かな}でる: to produce a tone

READINGS:
Can also be read おんしょく in more technical/academic contexts, but ねいろ is more common in everyday usage.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {音色|ねいろ} vs. {音質|おんしつ}
  - {音色|ねいろ}: timbre, the characteristic quality of a sound (often used for musical/aesthetic discussion)
  - {音質|おんしつ}: sound quality, often used for audio equipment and recordings

USAGE:
Applies to both musical instruments and voices. Often used with adjectives describing warmth, clarity, or emotional quality.
